categories.name: term_gloss_invented
categories.definition: The clause names or uses a term (a role, a label, a heading) without defining it; the reconstruction supplies a full definition, function, or characterization of that term drawn from background knowledge. Test: delete the phrase and the clause loses nothing; the phrase is "what X is", where the clause only says "X".
categories.boundary: Excludes phrases that define the term using content the spec itself supplies in a different clause — those are transplanted_from_elsewhere_in_spec (e.g. #u15 defines "user messages" with the wording of m0059).
examples: End user is a person who uses the model
Role identifies message source and authority

categories.name: transplanted_from_elsewhere_in_spec
categories.definition: The phrase states something this document plausibly does say — its own distinctive vocabulary, themes, or a sibling clause's content (irreversible side effects, chain of command, flourishing, uncertainty types, response-length adaptation) — but attaches it to a clause that does not carry it. Test: the claim reads like a correct summary of the spec, just of the wrong passage; often near-verbatim spec phrasing.
categories.boundary: Excludes generic assistant-policy commonplaces with no distinctive tie to this document's text — those are genre_boilerplate_import. The dividing question: could you locate the phrase's wording elsewhere in this spec, or only in the genre at large?
examples: Tool invocation causing difficult or impossible-to-reverse change
Assistant lacks sufficient knowledge or reasoning ability

categories.name: genre_boilerplate_import
categories.definition: Generic "what model specs usually require" filler: refuse harmful requests, consult qualified professionals, verify facts, deploy AI responsibly. Test: the phrase would be equally at home in any vendor's policy document; nothing anchors it to this clause or this spec's wording.
categories.boundary: Excludes claims echoing this spec's own distinctive sections or vocabulary (transplanted_from_elsewhere_in_spec), and generalizations launched from a worked example (rule_abstracted_from_example).
examples: Refusing or safely redirecting harmful requests
Independent verification before relying on facts is not stated.

categories.name: rule_abstracted_from_example
categories.definition: The clause is a worked example (good/bad comparison); the reconstruction asserts the general rule, principle, or motivation the example supposedly illustrates, which the example itself never states. Test: clause is an XML example block, and the phrase is an abstraction or rationale rather than anything in the dialogue.
categories.boundary: Excludes prose clauses whose stated rule is merely widened — that is scope_or_modality_inflation; here the source states no rule at all, only an instance.
examples: Creator control over intellectual property is not mentioned.
Provider revenue pursuit or provider-benefit motivation is not stated.
Synthetic speech characteristics are not mentioned.

categories.name: scope_or_modality_inflation
categories.definition: The clause's claim is present but upgraded in strength or reach: some->every, a specific prohibition -> a general one, a description or hypothetical -> an actual fact or requirement, an exception-laden rule -> an absolute. Test: the phrase entails the clause but not vice versa.
categories.boundary: Excludes additions that narrow or decorate rather than widen — "only", "specifically", invented qualifiers — which are spurious_specificity (the opposite direction of error).
examples: Every tool invocation causes an irreversible side effect
The model is pursuing these aims

categories.name: spurious_specificity
categories.definition: The reconstruction adds precision the clause never licenses: an "only"/"specifically" restriction, an invented qualifier or condition ("agreed acceptable limits", "significantly affecting an individual"), extra list members, or a substituted narrower term. Test: the clause entails a weaker/vaguer version of the phrase; the added specificity is fabricated.
categories.boundary: Excludes widenings (scope_or_modality_inflation). Where the invented specificity is itself a definition of a bare term, term_gloss_invented takes primary.
examples: Safe completions are limited to requests in harmful categories.

notes: Coverage verified programmatically: all 95 #u ids appear exactly once across assignments (93) and unclassified (2); per-category counts sum to 93. Judgement calls: (1) The corpus phrases come in two surface forms — positive assertions and meta-descriptions ("X is not stated/mentioned/required by the passage"). I treated the latter as naming the claim the reconstruction added (X) and classified X's relation to the clause, not the meta-sentence. (2) The transplant-vs-boilerplate line is the softest boundary: without re-reading the full spec I judged "would this wording be findable elsewhere in THIS spec" from the phrases' use of the document's distinctive vocabulary (bad surprises, chain of command, flourishing, types of uncertainty, follow-up messages); several boilerplate calls (#u60, #u65, #u76) could flip to transplant if the spec states them somewhere. (3) Repeated identical phrases attached to different clauses (#u1/#u25 transparency; #u26/#u29/#u36 irreversible tool effects; #u60/#u65 verification; #u3/#u6 end-user definition) strongly suggest the restricted notation has a small fixed inventory of expressible propositions, and decoding snaps clause content to the nearest inventory item — so most "fabrication" is not free invention but attraction toward a finite set of attractor claims. Consistent with that, whole-cloth invention is nearly absent: the dominant mass is transplanted_from_elsewhere_in_spec (39/95), i.e. true-of-the-document but false-of-the-clause. If categories were collapsed to one systematic transformation it would be "snap to nearest representable claim", with inflation (widen to a representable general form) and spurious specificity (narrow to a representable specific form) as the two directions of the snap. Doubts about the corpus: #u42 ("Assistant must not produce prohibited content") is arguably entailed by the clause plus the meaning of "prohibited", and #u14 ("User instructions have user authority") is near-tautological — these read more like annotator strictness than model fabrication. Unclassified: m0123#u24 ("Actions were not logically required" — an evaluative inference about necessity that fits no additive pattern) and m0276#u52 ("Interrupting the user" in a self-harm clause — no visible source in clause, spec theme, or genre).
